headline: Tools for cryo-EM fitting, MD refinement, and biomolecular structure prediction
label: Integrative Structural Biology Methods
summary: Recent preprints pair cryo-EM density fitting and differentiable restraints with force-field refinement against NMR and SAXS data.
synthesis: The common thread is coupling experimental structural data to computational modeling, emphasizing fitting, restraint, and validation over de novo prediction alone. In cryo-EM, PowerFit updates rigid-body fitting of atomic models into density maps, and a separate preprint combines iterative 3D classification, simulated-particle error quantification, and global thermodynamic modeling to resolve small energy differences in heterogeneous complexes. On the modeling side, RGI-Toolkit applies differentiable restraints across six diffusion-based predictors, and autofocusing finetunes MD force fields against NMR and SAXS constraints. Membrane and ligand work extends this to GalaxyMemMD's reproducible membrane-protein workflows, RLPF ligand trajectories, and DyME, the single published item, which couples high-throughput MD mutagenesis to recognition mimicry. A carbohydrate survey adds a validation caveat, asking whether pyranose ring distortions in the PDB reflect biology or experimental conditions.
